Brezovica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Brezovica, Slovakia

Not demolished. Brezovica's Jewish community, settled in the early 19th century, first worshipped in a private house before building a wooden synagogue in 1828; Rabbi Joseph Gazfried, author of Kesset ha-Sofer and other halachic works, served from 1843 to 1851, followed by a new synagogue in 1870. A 1925 fire destroyed several Jewish properties, including the rabbi's home. Deportations began in March 1942; some who evaded them joined the partisans. Only 5 Jews remained by 1948, and all were repatriated to Israel the following year. This cemetery, existing by the early 19th century with a matzeva dated 1822, was surveyed in 2007 by the Heritage Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries, which erected a stone wall around it.
